utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I think you need Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I will have her called in. DR. HANNE SOPHIE GREVE, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think you had almost concluded your testimony? Examined by MR. TIEGER, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Greve. You understand that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, before yesterday's adjournment we were discussing the military units which participated in the takeover and the cleansing of Opstina Prijedor, and we concluded yesterday as you reviewed several documents which detailed the involvement of different units. If I may, I would like to present you with one more document which I would like marked as Exhibit 119 for identification. (Document handed) Can you tell us what that document is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is a translation of an article in Kozarski Vjesnik. It is dated 26th August 1994 headlined "Without a battle lost".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does it concern the fighters of the 4th battalion of the 43rd Motorized Brigade in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document for admission, your Honour, as 119.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 119 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, can I ask you to turn to page 2 of that document, please? Looking at the middle of the page at the paragraph below the one which begins "July 4th 1992"; is there an indication of the areas where the 4th Battalion of the 43rd Motorized Brigade was involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is. It is stated that from May to December 1992 some formations of that battalion took part in cleansing the terrain in the direction of Kozarusa, Kozarac, Hambarine, Kurevo, Cela and Razboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I could ask that that Exhibit 116 be re-presented to the witness? Could you look at page 1, please, the second paragraph from the bottom? First of all, Dr. Greve, this is an article in honour of the 43rd Motorized Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does the article indicate in that second paragraph in the bottom of the page when that Brigade was mobilized and from what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. "The campaign of the 43rd Prijedor Motorized Brigade, however, began a year before that, more precisely on September 15th 1991 when the mobilization signal was received. The former 343rd Motorized Brigade left off its war assignment on September 18. It was on the main route of the then 5th Banja Luka (nowadays the first Krajina Corps): Strug, Okucani, Lipik, Pakrac".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So the 43rd Prijedor Motorized Brigade was initially mobilized in September 1991 as a 343rd of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was still the JNA on 15th September 1991, yes, as it was on 30th April 1992 when the Serbs took power by armed force in opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And that was a mobilization of persons to participate in the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, although it is not stated in this article that it was limited to the war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Which ethnic group or groups responded to that mobilization and which did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Primarily, those who responded were Serbs, the occasional non-Serb would respond as well, but the vast majority of non-Serbs did not respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So the 343rd Brigade of the JNA was a predominantly Serb unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was that the case when it announced itself as the 43rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is, however, my understanding that still at present the Serbs themselves do on occasions refer to the 343rd and the 43rd as interchangeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: May I ask now that document that Exhibit 118 be presented to the witness? Can you turn to the first page of that document, please? At the top of the page this document contains a recount of the 5th Kozara Brigade mobilization activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does it indicate when the 5th Kozara Brigade was mobilized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It refers to 9th July 1991 as being the date of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where did that assembly take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It took place in Kozarusa, meaning just two kilometres or a few hundred metres away from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would the same demographic conditions which you described a moment ago in connection with the mobilization of the 343rd Prijedor Brigade apply when the 5th Kozara Brigade was mobilized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, that is the case, yes. It is, however, not noted in this article for what purpose they were mobilized at that time. I do, however, in the context it can be read, assume that this is the part of this Brigade which later takes part in each and every battle listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were the military units which you have just indicated and the others you spoke about before also assisted by other armed personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. To my understanding, there were two military units headquartered, that is, two JNA military units headquartered in Prijedor, the one being this several time mentioned 343rd Motorized Brigade, the other being so-called partisan Brigade, the 11th partisan Brigade. A partisan Brigade is an ordinary designation for a light infantry Brigade. It is only with the memory of World War II and in honour of the partisans; that is the name used for this specific unit which is an ordinary unit or was an ordinary unit in the JNA. It was frequently characterised by being locally recruited so that the people, lightly armed, easy to mobilize, easy to move into a difficult terrain, would be very familiar with that particular area. So these were the two units located in Prijedor itself. There was a larger headquarter of the 5th Corps and actually a strong hold of the JNA, nothing wrong about that, but it used to be located in Banja Luka. And, as mentioned, there were numerous military and troop movements through Prijedor to reach the battlefields in Croatia, and there were a number of units that were moved into the area, located in the area, for a period of time to move on; some, however, did not move on. Some of those who came back or had stayed whether or not they , for the event they could possibly be used in Croatia, some of these moved back. It is not to me fully clear exactly which were the units that moved back and which did not. But it is known that there were huge troop movements even in early May 1992. This is the time when the Serbs had taken power in Prijedor, and people would say in the Kozarac area where the main highway to Banja Luka is, that heavy equipment would pass that road for about half an hour at the time, meaning there were huge movements of military equipment that had not been moved far away at all events. When the attack started, it was on Kozarac area in particular. It was used a lot of heavy equipment, heavy artillery, in particular, and it had been placed almost all around the area of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were the military units which participated in the cleansing assisted by the police as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were assisted by the police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look once again at Exhibit 93? Looking quickly at the first page of Exhibit 93, is that an article which celebrates the day of the security services of the republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It is called the "Blue Angels" which has some reference to their uniform. The ordinary police uniform would be blue and the Serb police uniform normally would be light blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Looking at the top of page 2 of that document, is there any indication by Serbian officials that there was participation and co-operation between the police and the military forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is explicitly stated that things are happening in co-operation with the police of Banja Luka, Kozarac, Dubica and Sanski Most, the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does it indicate that the police of Prijedor also participated in that effort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the policemen from Prijedor is also specifically listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In addition to the military forces, the Police Forces, were paramilitary forces also involved in the cleansing of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How were they recognisable or distinguishable from the other forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not wearing the same uniforms always; in part they did, in part they did not. That is to say a number of them would wear the Kokarda, which is this special Cheknik hat. If my memory serves me right, there is an excellent picture of that in the film which was shown to you during Dr. Gow's testimony. I think it is related to when Seselj is speaking, and then you will have just after a few people with the Kokarda and the three fingers lifted. I do not know if that footage could be shown again, but the Kokarda is a very special hat used by the paramilitary Chetnik groups. There are different insignias being used; some are recognised as being the insignia of the JNA; some are recognised as being the former insignia of the JNA from which the five pointed star, the red star, has been removed. I should add that in the former Yugoslavia it used to be 24 months of military service in the early 80s. Then it was reduced to 18 months. I do not know if it was also reduced to 15 months before it came down to 12 months, but it means that almost all males above a certain age had been wearing this particular uniform for a considerable period of time themselves, meaning that they were not asked to identify some alien uniform, but it was the very clothing they had been wearing themselves, the signs and insignias with which they were very familiar indeed. But they also saw a number of insignias new to them, such as the one you saw on the film when this paramilitary unit took over the TV relay station on Mount Kozara. It is actually located at Mali Vis or Lisnija which is a few kilometres up from Lamovita, not far from Omarska. But there you saw the new Yugoslav flag and a wolf within it. You would see such insignias -- I am not familiar with exactly this insignia having been seen in the onslaught of Prijedor, Kozarac or on the left side of the River Sana, but they would see the double headed eagle; they would see the cross with the four Cs; they would see a number of berets which were not known to them as being ordinary berets of the JNA units involved, and they would see a lot of rag tag uniforms not easily distinguished. But I should mention that a number of people also in the proper JNA forces, or later what is called the Serbian army, did not wear complete uniforms. There were a shortage of uniforms so sometimes they would lack the military trousers or shoes or boots or some part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked for identification as Exhibit 120? (Document handed). (To the witness): Dr. Greve, does Exhibit 120 depict one of the insignias you have referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, it depicts one presentation of what is an insignia referred to. This is the old Royal Emblem, to my understanding. It is the double headed eagle and it is the cross with the four Cs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 120 will be admitted. But what is this now? Is this a part of the uniform of the JNA, is that your testimony, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is a Chetnik insignia, if I may show you this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Chetnik"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Chetnik", your Honours, deserves perhaps a little bit of explanation. It is not a very precise name. That is to say, Chetniks in the old time were heroes of the people defending the local people from outside robbers, etc. They were veterans from World War I, and they were appreciated as having fought on the right side. During World War II, there were numerous groups calling themselves Chetniks, some were partisans and some joined hands with the Nazis. The main Chetnik movement under the leadership of Drazan Mihajlovic was a Chetnik movement that joined hands with the Nazis, the Germans, the Austrians, the Ustashas and engaged themselves in killing off both their own people and other people in the former Yugoslavia. "Chetnik" as a name today does give rise to different feelings; some have very good feelings linked to it, but the way it is being used in this present conflict, it has become the symbol of the new nationalistic very right wing representatives of the war. As a paramilitary group, they have got a reputation as being a very brutal, right wing group that people are very afraid of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Led by whom and whoever the person would be is that person from Bosnia-Herzegovina or Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume it is correct, and my understanding of this is slightly limited, that there are several groups that call themselves "Chetniks". It is like a generic term. There are a number of groups, such as Arkan's group, Seselj's group, etc., with leaders in Serbia proper who will be close to being identified as being Chetniks. If that is correct, or if actually the Chetniks should be outside that groups as well, it may be a matter of how you would want to identify Chetniks, but seeing as a symbol, this is carried by many. This is, if I may draw your Honour's attention to this particular presentation, this is the Byzantine double-headed eagle, the Royal Symbol, the eagle able to keep watch both to the east and the west at the same time, or it may have other good meanings as well, and it is the cross with four Cs. That is, it is the old coat of arms It is disputed whether what now appears as four Cyrillic Cs, in our Latin alphabet it will be S, if that was actually Cs or it was only a reflection of the cross to sort of make the cross more visible to at the time a highly illiterate public. However, now the Cs are interpreted as meaning only unity may serve, save the Serbs, or it is translated as being St. Sava is the patron saint of the Serbs. But you will see a variety of presentations of this. Possibly it was difficult to recognise, but on the video you were presented with yesterday from Kozarac there were a number of just simple crosses and four sharp pointed Cs which is a variation of this. A number of groups that people considered to be Chetnik groups, if I may phrase it this way, will carry the silhouette of the double-headed eagle and have just the simple cross with simple Cs, meaning S in our Latin alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, if I can ask you a couple of questions about what you have just testified to? Prior to the 1990s, the most recent incarnation or embodiment of Chetniks was associated with World War II?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Among the major group calling itself Chetniks was an extreme nationalist group which cooperated with the Nazis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was actually the royalist wing and it was led by Drazan Mihajlovic, and that was the reason why Tito and his partisans in 1943, at the end of 1943, decided to declare this as a purely Nazi extreme group with whom they would not co-operate, and which eventually led Churchill to break all relations with the same group. Drazan Mihajlovic was executed after World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After World War II, were Chetnik symbols and Chetnik songs banned in former Yugoslavia as nationalist symbols and propaganda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were, and like the Ustasha symbols, and one may mention that on buses in the former Yugoslavia, you would have small notices that would say: "In case you see someone who behaved in a manner that may lead to ethnic hatred etc., please call this telephone number and report"; whereas we would perhaps in a bus be advised of whom to call in case of fire or an accident or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the late 1980s and early 1990s were the Chetnik symbols and songs resurrected by certain extremist, nationalist groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time that really happened was at the celebration at Kosovo Polje in 1989. It is also shown in the film "The Fall of Yugoslavia".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were those groups associated with the concept and promotion of a greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. When Tito broke with all these Chetnik movements under Drazan Mihajlovic, they particularly stated that one of the main aims of that movement had been greater Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did some of those groups form paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were among some of those groups the ones led by Seselj and Arkan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As earlier mentioned, it may be correct to put Arkan and Seselj's groups within a wider frame of Chetnik groups, but it may also be possible to make more narrow determination of Chetnik, but they are almost on the same line, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Among the emblems or insignias used by those groups, would be the one depicted on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That could come up among them, yes . I should, perhaps, add that the eagle and the cross with the four Cs may not necessarily go together. This was the one representation and that is the old Royal symbol. They could be used separately and just as silhouettes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were persons from Serbia involved in these paramilitary groups which operated in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the people they could hear from, the language they spoke, that they were speaking Ijekavian which is easily distinguished from their own language and which means that the people originate from an area in Serbia proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, is it possible to calculate or know exactly how many people, Muslims and Croats, were killed during the cleansing of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not possible to calculate at this stage, that is to say, I assume that demographers will be able to do this after some more time, but it has not been possible for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that a figure which is in the tens, the hundreds, the thousands or is there any way of giving the court some general sense of the victims of the cleansings in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again it is difficult to say, state numbers exactly, but the population was in about a year's time reduced by 53,000 people and, I am afraid, I think the true figure is in tens of thousands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you share with the court some of the factors which assist in gauging the extent of the destruction in opstina Prijedor and the killing in opstina Prijedor? You indicated that 53,000 people were gone from the area in a short time. Did the Serbian authorities indicate how many people were processed for deportation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is one indication. The Serb authorities in Srpska opstina Prijedor were very keen to have the papers and records in shape and all that, so they wanted everyone to sign an exit visa, or an application for an exit visa, where they handed over all their property and they have later, when confronted with how many died, that question from the media, they have been very eager to tell the press that actually these people left voluntarily and wanted to seek a better future elsewhere and "we", as they say, showed the press 20,000 such applications, or actually applications of this character with reference to 20,000 people. But, of course, that make the question, and then what about the 53,000 others? Of course, there must have been a number who have left without signing. One other way of coming closer to understand the magnitude of this is, perhaps, that the male group between 12, 15 and 55, 60, 65, perhaps, must have been, if we take that in a normal population, about half and half of women and men, perhaps between one-third and one-fourth underneath the age of 15, we have some very broad understanding of the number of males that must have been in this group. We do, however, know that eventually when the males had been segregated from the women's group and taken to the camps, Keraterm and Omarska, they were proceeding from these camps not many thousands people; approximately 1600 via Manjaca, just take a high number and say 2,000 to Trnopolje from Omarska -- I think that is far too high but just take a high number -- say they took 1400 from Keraterm -- again a high number -- we have 5,000. I cannot, I am sorry about it, I cannot make good, proper, solid estimates, but I think there are very good indications in the very limited numbers of people who left. But that is all I can say on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First, your Honour, may Exhibit 92 be presented to the witness once more? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, Exhibit 92 is an interview with Simo Drljaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the interview several times referred to when he is appointed Vice Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you would look at the fourth paragraph on page 2 and tell us whether there is a reference by Simo Drljaca to the number of people who were processed for so-called immigration A.Yes, in this interview, Simo Drljaca, head of the Serbian police, is referring to as to the extensive work, and it is the understanding from all available information that this work was really extensive, performed by the administrative, legislative bodies. It is enough to say that more than 20,000 cases of immigration by Muslim and Croat citizens were registered. Initially, the officials when confronted by foreign press would state that there were some casualties, a few thousand, and there were so many extremists so they had to fight them. But after about a year's time, there is no more such references, then they have chosen another line of communication and this line of communication is that these people were departing on their own initiative seeking a better future in different other countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But initially Serbian officials in opstina Prijedor acknowledged to enquiring journalists that thousands of people had been killed, although they characterised them as extremists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was the cleansing of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The cleansing of Kozarac, the attack started on 24th May 1992, and it continued for about a month's time or so, that is, there were the occasional round up going on for quite some time, but the main achievements were made within two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the Serbian army still picking up bodies in July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they said they had a heavy task in picking up bodies in the middle of the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked for identification as Exhibit 121? (Document handed). (To the witness): Dr. Greve, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This, your Honours, is again an article published in Kozarski Vjesnik. It is dated 10th July 1992, and it is headlined "New authorities beginning functioning in Kozarac".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender 121 for admission, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 121 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, does this article concern the tasks and responsibilities awaiting the new military and civilian authorities in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: According to the Commander of a unit responsible for such things in that area, what are the primary tasks in Kozarac at the beginning of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The primary tasks as of 10th July 1992 are to capture the remaining small groups of Muslim extremists, to remove the corpses and to round up the loose cattle. This is mid summer and it is very hot in the area, and it is also known that a number of people would risk their life in order to try to retrieve dead relatives and try to give them a funeral high enough to bury their relatives, even if that meant they would have to pay with their lives for so doing, so many must have been removed long before this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, in addition to the deaths of Muslims and Croats in the opstina, what happened to the physical centres of the Muslim and Croat community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were raised to the ground. Essentially, they were blown up, they were wiped out. Initially, it was told to the press that all the high rise buildings, such as mosques, minarets, churches had to be torn down because it could be an advantage position for snipers, but they did not tear down other high rise buildings, or high rise meaning more than one storey, two storeys.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were there many mosques in the Prijedor opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were quite a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And religious institutions, educational centres, community buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was also the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were those the targets of destruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What about the remaining property of the Muslim and Croat community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of that was looted and taken over. Officially, it was documented that they had handed it over, signing exit applications for exit visas, but all their property was taken over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as Exhibit 122 for identification, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is acknowledged by the Serb authorities that this was billions of dinar worth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me just a ask a question about the last exhibit that was on the monitor, 121: It says: "Captain Mirko Savanovic, Commander of the unit responsible for this area". Yesterday I am sure you told us about Captain Savanovic and I may have just forgotten -- did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then I did not forget. Tell us, who is he and what does this mean, "of the unit responsible for the area"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with Captain Mirko Savanovic prior to this report. I think he may have been appointed local Commander and he could have been a Commander previously. I assume that must have been the case, but I have no specific information concerning him prior to this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what unit is being referred to, by number? I mean, is this still the 43rd or 243rd?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 343rd, excuse me, or 43rd; you said they were used interchangeably. Do you know whether the unit that is referred is one of those two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am afraid I do not know that. This is in a period when most of the people are, unfortunately, the non-Serbs are out of opstina Prijedor, and this is a time when local command has not been easy to establish beyond what has been available through media communications and top level appointments which has been confirmed also outside of Prijedor. So, although certain names have been mentioned on occasions, I do not have firm information of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can I ask you to look at Exhibit 122? What is this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik. It is dated 30th July 1993. It is called "On the loot of public property".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender this document as 122 for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 122 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, can I direct your attention to the last paragraph of the first page? First of all, does the article contain an interview or a report from Bogdan Delic, the new head of public security station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. He was the man to follow Simo Drljaca when Drljaca was promoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does he indicate what happened to the Muslim and Croat community of opstina Prijedor and to their property?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is in the last paragraph referring to that about 50,000 people of other ethnic origins used to live within the territory of the municipality of Prijedor. "The total of their property has been unofficially estimated at several billion deutschemarks. A smaller proportion of that property was destroyed during the military operations, but most of it was saved". Then he is complaining about this post being available to the community and then being looted by Serbian officials. If I may, as it may have catched the eye of your Honours, mention that when "Keraterm" is used in the line above and said "emptied overnight", "Keraterm" in this context means that it was used as a storage area. So, "Keraterm" in this context is not reference to the camp which we were describing yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So this article contains Bogdan Delic's complaints about the loot of public property?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That public property is the property unofficially estimated at several billion deutschemarks which belonged to the 50,000 people of other ethnic origins who formerly lived in the territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and there are or articles and other reports when he speaks to outsiders saying that everything from what were in their houses to their cars, to their cattle, to their sawmills, to their production units, to their bank accounts, everything is gone, which has also torn apart the social fabric in opstina Prijedor, which is one reason why he is addressing this issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not need to ask too many questions, but let me if I can understand. From your testimony yesterday I believe you said that there were 112,000 persons -- that was the population of the Prijedor opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then you told us there was a percentage of Muslim, Croats and Serbs and they were 40 something, there were very close with the Serbs and Muslims. Tell me again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were 44 per cent Muslims; 42.5 per cent Serbs; 5.6 per cent Croats; 5.7 per cent calling themselves Yugoslavs and 2.2 per cent aliens; the Yugoslavs being those who found it convenient, mixed descent or for political reasons, to confirm their faith in the Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am trying to get a fix, I suppose, on the number of persons of non-Serb origin who left the area. This last Exhibit 122 said that 50,000 persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, if I may? I am sorry to interrupt but, your Honour, I have an exhibit which may be of some assistance to the court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I just do not understand because earlier you said probably the population was reduced by 53,000, but you did not know how many had been cleansed and this exhibit says 50,000, and then when I remember what you testified to yesterday, the numbers do not mix, they do not fit for me -- will it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will, your Honour, if I am able to show you the next exhibit, because I thought these figures would be inconvenient to deal with without having them, sort of, spelled out on paper. So this was prepared by me for that reason. If I may, your Honours, when I say "cleansed" I mean both killed and deported. When I tried to estimate numbers this morning, it was of people killed. That is to say, trying to estimate how many within the group of 53,000 who may have been killed in the process. That is what is so very difficult. To estimate the numbers of those who have left or are out is not difficult, according to the Serbian official figures for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This exhibit is called out of order for the benefit of Defence document 51, and this will be Exhibit 123. (Document handed). (To the witness): Dr. Greve, this is the comparison chart that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it based on the official census of 1991 and the figures which appeared in the Kozarski Vjesnik in 1993 unofficially estimating the number of people in the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is called unofficial census results.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The title of that article is "Who we are"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Who we are and how many", yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have a question for the Prosecution. Is the source of the article in the Kozarski Vjesnik one of the other exhibits, that is, the article dated July 2nd 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: OK, no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 123 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you want to show the article first?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is already in evidence. Dr. Greve, using Exhibit 123, can you explain the population changes within opstina Prijedor between 1991 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the column to your left, your Honours, will be the one based on the census, according to which the Serbs who were 42.5 per cent were 47,581 people. In 1993, according to this newspaper article, the number of Serbs in the area was or were 53,637. That is, there had been some new arrivals to the area, their number being 6,056. The Muslims, on the other hand, who in 1991 had been the largest ethnic group, 44 per cent of the population, were 49,351. In 1993, their number had been reduced to 6,124. That is, the reduction was 43,227. The Croats, who were 5.6 per cent in 1991, then being 6,316 were in 1993 counted to be 3,169; a reduction of 3,147. I should add that it is me who have been calculating the reduction for the newcomers of the Serbs, but it is just calculations based on the figures given. Others, which is the group consisting both of Yugoslavs and aliens, as the newspaper article of 1993 do not distinguish between these groups, were 9,295, that is, 5.7 per cent Yugoslavs and 2.2 per cent aliens. In 1993, their number was reduced to 2,622, that is, a reduction of 6,673 and, if one adds up the reductions, it is just above 53,000. I hope this will answer to your questions, your Honour, but if you would like me to explain it any more, I am happy to try that. For my own needs, I thought it was much easier to see it visualised like this. That is why I had it prepared.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you assume that 20,000 were processed for immigration, and if you then subtracted that number, the 20,000 from the number of reduction, would you then assume that 30,000 plus had disappeared by other means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I will say is that the Serb officials themselves say that they can document the 20,000 left and they were very keen on documenting this, to the point that the International Committee of the Red Cross urged and advised people to give up everything, all their material goods, and their right to stay in their homeland or, rather, to stay in opstina Prijedor which to them was very important. So, what happened to the 33,000, history will probably teach us and the demographers, but I think the number of people killed is considerable. I am sure some left without signing papers, I am sure some were able to, as the newspaper articles say, leave in Serb cars or with Serb identities or in coffins, but it sounds very cumbersome and I do not think there were many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: That means that those who fled rather than seeking permission would not be included in the 20,000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, but it was not easy to flee this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was encircled and those who were rounded up in nearby opstinas were handed back and even the UN turned people back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One short question, Dr. Greve: the group labelled "others", are those people who declared themselves as Yugoslav?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does meaning they could belong to any other groups, Serbs, Muslims, Croats; they were unlikely to be aliens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document as 124 for identification and indicate, for the benefit of the Defence and the court, I spoke too soon about the admission of the other source for the document now in evidence and we will tender that now. (To the witness): What is 124, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the article which the figures were based on printed in Kozarski Vjesnik, 2nd July 1993. It is titled "Unofficial census results. Who are we and how many?"

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just a minute, your Honour. Could you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It will be document 7 on your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 124 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Would you view that document briefly? Dr. Greve, this is an article published in Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Which contains the unofficial census results ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: -- prior to their official publication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This is the document on which the previous document is partially based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, for those 6,000 or so Muslims and 3,000 or so Croats who remained in Prijedor after the cleansings, what were conditions like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conditions were very, very severe, that is, now there was a period of time when they were almost lawless; they were called to do dangerous and difficult work; they had difficulties in buying food; they would be harassed; they had difficulties in going outside their houses and all the time some people were killed. Among this group there were many elderly couples and this really reached a peak in early 1994. I think it is the Herald Tribune that in its issue of 19th to 20th March 1992 refers to the fact that 1,000 people came forward to UNHCR and asked to be moved, all of them, it was too small, the remaining Muslim villages and one small remaining gypsy village, and a little later ICRC, the same month, reported that only on 29th and 30th March 1994, 20 people were killed and that is a lot of people in any small community at one time. This made both UNHCR and ICRC urge the Bosnian Serb authorities to let them evacuate every single remaining non-Serb from Srpska opstina Prijedor. It was refused, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, you refer to 20 people killed; what nationality or ethnic group did those people belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats, they were identified as. It was among this group numbers were killed as their houses were set on fire or they were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as Exhibit 125 for identification? It is Defence document No. 33. (Document handed). (To the witness): Dr. Greve, first of all, let me ask you to look at that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document that dates back to 3rd October 1992. It is a press release by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It is entitled "Saving lives in Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is 125, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 125 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, would you direct your attention to page 2 of that document, please? This is an ICRC report in the fall of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Shortly after the events which you have just described, you described during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the intensive -- just after the intensive cleansing period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does the ICRC refer to its findings during that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does and it is using an alarming language.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How do they describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They refer to the most basic principle of International Humanitarian Law continue to be ignored in the field -- not violated, ignored.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do they indicate the conditions for people continuing to remain in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How do they describe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it starts with describing what has happened during the so-called ethnic cleansing where tens of thousands, or hundreds actually as it came out, have been forcibly displaced in inhumane conditions. Hundreds and even thousands have died in that process. This is for Bosnia-Herzegovina at large. It is not specific reference to Prijedor, I should add. It is said that acts of (indecipherable) and indiscriminate attacks have been carried out on a massive scale; entire regions have been inaccessible to humanitarian organisations for months and some still are at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do they then talk about the circumstances for those persons who remained in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They do. They say that, "Moreover, the ICRC is convinced that under cover of a policy of 'ethnic cleansing' tens of thousands of members of minority groups in areas controlled by the parties are still at the mercy of repressive measures applied locally in accordance with a discriminatory ideology. It is said that these practices are inadmissible. The parties to the conflict cannot continue to claim that such acts are carried out by groups of irregulars, since those groups operate in areas which have been under the party's military control for months".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like you to move from October 1992 to May 1993. I would ask that this document be marked as Exhibit 126 for identification. (Document handed). What is this document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is another communication to the press issued by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It is dated 7th May 1993 and headlined "Bosnia-Herzegovina, minorities in Banja Luka in danger".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 126 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, in this document does the ICRC indicate the conditions for remaining civilians in the Banja Luka area in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they do. "The civilian population is under constant pressure by armed groups who repeatedly beat, rob and threaten persons belonging to minorities. The houses of such persons in Banja Luka and nearby villages are regularly attacked and burned down by uncontrolled elements". The Red Cross in this period refers, it is known from the different other contexts to Banja Luka area as including also Prijedor -- opstina Prijedor, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In that connection I would ask you to look at a document we will mark for identification as 127. (Document handed). Dr. Greve, what is Exhibit 127?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also a press release issued by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It is dated 31st March 1994. It is issued in Geneva where ICRC is headquartered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does it concern a specific opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It concerns opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What is the source of that concern, what is the cause of that concern, in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this case it is reported that "nine Muslims civilians have been murdered in the last two days".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 127 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Does the ICRC indicate whether or not the murders of nine Muslim civilians in two days in March of '94 are just the confirmed reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are only the confirmed reports, yes. The ICRC later referred to named lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did the ICRC condemn these acts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did they attempt to take some action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took some very strong action. They sent the head of ICRC to negotiate with Milosevic in Belgrade and negotiate to have them entitled to evacuate the entire remaining population after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does the document refer to a specific message sent to any Serbian leader?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was requested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Requested "immediate measures to restore security to the Prijedor area and calling for an end to such intolerable acts of violence against minority population groups". But it was so violent at this time that this was not considered enough. They sent their head of the delegation to Belgrade to negotiate, to have them out and Milosevic agreed and Karadzic refused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not see that. Where in the exhibit is it indicated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not listed here. It will come, I think, in the next exhibit. I was perhaps -- or the next exhibit will not refer to the negotiations but to the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like this marked as Exhibit 128 for identification, please. (Document handed). (To the witness): What is this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is information to the press from the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender this document for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 128 will be admitted. We will see the date on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is issued in Zagreb, 7th April 1994, your Honour. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, does this document indicate the outcome of the ICRC's concern and efforts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does. It is indicating that the International Committee of the Red Cross have taken immediate steps to increase its monitoring of the protection of minority groups in the northern Bosnian town of Prijedor. "These steps have been taken following the authority's rejections of the ICRC plan to evacuate all members of the minority population who wish to leave the area".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did the ICRC at that time attempt to visit Prijedor as frequently as possible to monitor the condition that was referred to in the previous exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does this document reflect the negotiations that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is only a few days between the previous press release and the appeal to Karadzic, and this press release, and in between there have been negotiations in Belgrade and there have been refusal by Karadzic to let the people get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That document also indicates, that is, the previous exhibit, that an urgent message was sent to Dr. Karadzic requesting immediate measures to restore security to the Prijedor area and calling for an end to the intolerable acts which have been described in the previous ICRC press releases and statements; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to have this document marked as Exhibit 129 for identification and it is Defence 12. (Document handed). (To the witness): What is this document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik. It is dated 26th November 1993 entitled "Shoulder to shoulder with the army".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 129 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, does this article recount a celebration and recollection of the war efforts of the policemen of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. "Boys in blue" is again a reference to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: War efforts which you have described to us in your testimony in connection with the armed takeover and cleansing of opstina Prijedor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and running of camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: On this occasion were awards bestowed on members of the police department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was an award bestowed on Simo Drljaca, the Chief of Police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who presented that award to Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is listed that the President of Republika Srpska, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, awarded the medal, Petar Mrkonjic, to the police station in Prijedor, and Karadordeva -- I should perhaps not try to read this in Serbo-Croatian, I apologise -- to the former head and now assistant in the Ministry of the Interior, Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Greve. I have no additional questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have no additional questions of Dr. Greve. Is there any cross? We will stand in recess for 20 minutes now and then you can organise your cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, I have some questions to ask you and perhaps if we can start with Exhibit 123 which you have referred to toward the end of your testimony. It is the population change from what we have described as the official census in 1991 and the unofficial census in 1993. First of all, in relation to the official census in 1991, that was undertaken by usual governmental agencies, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By the department responsible in Prijedor for recording the people within the district?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was conducted in the former Yugoslavia according to procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. What we have in 1993 which has been described as the unofficial census, how did that take place? How was that recorded? Who undertook that obligation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That obligation was undertaken by the Serbian authorities then in power in Srpska opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. So that derived from the Prijedor district. Do you know who actually undertook it and why it is called "unofficial"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who took it or undertook to arrange it. I assume that it could have been called an unofficial census because it was not a year of an official census, but that is just a guess on my part. My main concern with these figures is that these are the only figures produced by the authorities in Srpska opstina Prijedor to explain to the population who they are and how many they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. These figures derived from that article you referred to in the newspaper, Kozarski Vjesnik, under that title "Unofficial census results; who are we and how many?" but they were not provided from an official governmental document from the region or from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If by "region" you refer to Banja Luka, they are not, to my knowledge, confirmed at the time of the newspaper article by Banja Luka. However, I have related to these figures also for the reason that when UNHCR and ICRC were able to get into this area, which was after the main phase of the so-called ethnic cleansing, they would give aid, and they would ask the Serbian authorities how many aid should be provided. Figures given to the aid community as represented by ICRC and UNHCR were slightly lower than these figures, meaning that when ICRC asked for total evacuation, the estimate was that the remaining non-Serbian population was around 9,000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So for the provision of aid was the ICRC informed of the ethnic composition of the local population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my understanding that they were informed of how many target groups would be there to receive aid, but of course at this time also Serbian people would have some aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you are referring to aid that is being supplied by the ICRC, that would of course be based upon a population, a group of people, that required aid. If aid was not required, then they would not be within the ICRC figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ICRC's main function, if I may, is to protect civilians, inter alia, in the course of armed conflict. Geneva Convention IV relates to this. The main function of aid assistance to be provided by ICRC in this region was to look after threatened minority groups, for what reason they needed to have an almost exact number of these people, and to know where they could find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So were the figures that were supplied to the ICRC their own figures, or figures that had been supplied by the opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This I cannot answer for the reason that ICRC will not share these kinds of exchanges in the process. What I know is this figure as having been published, and I know the figure which ICRC refers to when ICRC ask to move everyone out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking at these figures and we see the column "New arrivals", and there is a figure slightly over 6,000 indicating new arrivals of Serbs, could they also have been people formerly under the "Others" column who perhaps switched or adopted their identity of the Serb people, so that they expressed themselves as being Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so. If I may, I would like perhaps to have this newspaper article again because it explicitly refers to more than 5,000 of these people as refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 124. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tieger; perhaps if we can have that produced?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It might help if we had the exhibits on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honours -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I realise you have to look at it, but we can follow your cross-examination better, I think, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does your Honour have this bundle of exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, we have what was admitted yesterday, yes, we do, but of course the population figures came in today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They have not been provided yet to you?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry. I did not appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will have no difficulties, your Honour, in reading from both sides. It was only when it was far away I had every difficulty with it. MR. KAY (To the witness): Yes, Dr. Greve, we have there the article from Kozarski Vjesnik dated 2nd July 1993. You wanted to look specifically at the "Others" figure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and my reference would be to the last paragraph in which it is stated that, "5,451 inhabitants of Prijedor are resettled persons", meaning people who are settled from outside, "of which 5,037 have refugee status". I cannot read this in any way other way than meaning that this is not simply a redeclaration by people who have called themselves "Yugoslavs" previously and that has been recorded as "Others", and now moved up as "New arrivals". If it could include the odd exception, I would not exclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, because it is not inconceivable that people chose, perhaps, to redefine their ethnic background and there would be no obstruction to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, Serbs who had declared themselves as Yugoslavs were, nonetheless, considered Serbs, that is, participated in, were mobilized into army Reserve forces, etc. So, it was not disqualifying in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, but that is a slightly different issue, is it not, as to whether they were accepted for mobilization compared with whether they are included within the census returns or the census figures that we have? Their acceptability for military service is a rather different issue, is it not, from whether they would be within a particular category of this so-called unofficial census?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a relative slightly different issue. However, I think it is correct to take the words of the article as they are, indicating that people are resettled in Srpska opstina Prijedor and qualify, as the local authorities see it, as refugees and the number in this category being a minimum of 5,037.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. I notice from the article of Exhibit 124 that it refers to the Prijedor municipality, and your column of figures, Exhibit 123, refers to the opstina Prijedor. Are we dealing here in the actual article with Prijedor town rather than the district of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We are dealing here with the opstina Prijedor. "Opstina" is sometimes translated as municipality, sometimes as a district.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For the overall district of opstina Prijedor, are not these figures slightly low? Would not these figures perhaps apply to Prijedor town itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not. If I may, "opstina" may be translated as district or municipality, but there is no such thing as "district opstina" Prijedor. The entity, the district entity, or the municipality entity, including the town of Prijedor and the surrounding areas, is referred to as the "opstina", and this is not confined to the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It refers to numbers of households as being 19,767. Would you say then that this census refers to the total number of households that were surveyed for the census in the opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will say that this article refers to the entire remaining number of households in Srpska opstina Prijedor and, as the film from Kozarac area would show, there are immense destruction in the Kozarac area, as it is in the Ljubija area. There are the odd exceptions, Serb houses remaining, the orthodox churches standing, but there are an immense number of houses physically destroyed. For what reason, more recently, when new arrivals have come into Prijedor after what happened in August last year in Croatian Krajina, newcomers have not so much been given houses to settle in but been asked to stay in schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, you yourself said yesterday that, in fact, there was a great deal of destruction after the original conflict within Kozarac; there were looters, there were people pillaging properties and damaging them which took place in the months and, indeed, years afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not able to confirm that it took place in years afterwards. To my understanding from those who have been in the area, it took place in the second half of 1992, essentially.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, you have not actually been to this district, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Even to this day, if people were still plundering houses, ripping cable out of walls, taking pipes from buildings, that kind of activity and event would not be something that you would know about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not if it happened on a small scale. I have, as rightly stated, not been to Prijedor, but there have been aid agencies in particular in this area and they have reported the main part of the destruction as having taken place just subsequent to the so-called ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because one of the problems that this district was faced with was refugees from other areas of the former Yugoslavia also coming within its district, and they themselves requiring housing, requiring to get their hands on property to build shelter, to provide themselves with materials to rebuild. For that they looked upon houses that had already been damaged or were abandoned; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we have to be very clear about which period of time we are talking about. After the war in Croatia, four areas (as marked yellow on one of the exhibits previously) were ethnically cleansed with the consequence that those remaining were Serbs. The areas around Prijedor were ethnically cleansed with the consequence that those who remained were Serbs. So, if your question is when the refugees come to opstina Prijedor, I would perhaps ask you to tell me what time period you are focusing on and which refugees, as I myself see it a big difference after August 1995 which is much after the so-called ethnic cleansing of Prijedor and what happened back in 1991, 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is the case, is it not, that in 1992 there were Serb refugees who were coming into this area from other parts of the former Yugoslavia? For instance, Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For instance, Sanski Most is not an example. Sanski Most became an ethnically cleansed Serbian controlled area. So if we talk of refugees, we talk of central Bosnian refugees, we talk of people, we talk about people who have crossed the front line close to Travnik, Tobe(?), Doboj, Maglaj, in those areas, and they had a long distance to move to come to Prijedor. But, as this article indicates, in 1993 there had indeed been some newcomers, their number was low.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The figures that you have compiled here indicate over 6,000 new arrivals being Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That would rather indicate that they are refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I accept that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I consider that to be a lower figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That may be a matter of judgment, as to whether that is high or low. But in 1992 there were people who were coming from Bihac, for instance; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Bihac, that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you yourself in 1992, of course, were not in Europe in the second half of 1992; you were in Cambodia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and until what period in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came back to Europe the 9th to 4th February.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, looking at your column of figures on Exhibit 123, and taking perhaps a middle year which is not in these columns of 1992, before the conflict started, in fact people were leaving the area generally, people were unhappy with the mood between the ethnic groups and people were perhaps returning to their own areas if they were in Croatia to other parts of the former Yugoslavia and Serbs, indeed, leaving the area to go, for instance, to Belgrade; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a statement on your part ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and I am not able to confirm if Serbs went to Belgrade. There have been movements, yes, but there are no reports of any large movements in early 1992, meaning prior to 30th April. Actually, there were restrictions on movement already a month or one-and-a-half months prior to this, but I will not exclude that there were some movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was a bus service to Belgrade that operated regularly from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the bus service went from Prijedor Auto Transport Prijedor, to Banja Luka and from Banja Luka there were onward transport, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was the railway which we have referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which did go the whole way to Sarajevo and to Zagreb or vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are, of course, the roads and the auto routes which cover the maps that we have seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if we leave this area then and move on to other general matters. In your evidence over the last two days you have referred to propaganda that was presented to the local population and had been instrumental in affecting their views?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By "propaganda" we talk about newspapers, we talk about radio, we talk about television, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there any other organs of propaganda that were being used to influence the local population, statements from the local government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there may have been statements from the local government and, to my knowledge, statements from the local legally elected government all went to the effect: "Remember World War II. Remember the brotherhood. Remember the special fate of this particular area. Remember that we are all brothers. We are intermarried. We have lived in peace for 50 years. Whatever happens elsewhere, we do not have to fear anything".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was a time as well of political birth in many respects of various parties, as a democracy from a previously totalitarian state was flowering, was coming into existence for the first time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that is the character of building a democracy, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and I take that really from the terms of your evidence yesterday when you were dealing with this subject, and you said that it was difficult for people who had not had experience or political democracy before to adjust to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What we had here then is a selection of political parties, SDS, the SDA, HDZ, all competing for power and influence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Let me, though, point out that when you mentioned HDZ they have two members of the Assembly. So, obviously both the Reformists, the Liberal Party and others who had 30 seats must have received also a sizeable proportion of votes. It is only -- I do not know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the influence of the HDZ was not particularly significant in this area as it might have been in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have here then the two main political parties of the SDS and the SDA competing, and their sources of information coming, presumably, from different places. The SDS, where would you say its information was coming from, how it was fighting its political campaign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The SDS, meaning the Serb Democratic Party, was Serb Democratic Party in Bosnia-Herzegovina with close links to Serbs elsewhere, but the central location of the SDS in Bosnia-Herzegovina was Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The SDA, its information and its political campaign, where would you say that that was originating from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Similarly I would say that the SDA, meaning the party for Democratic Action which had many Muslim followers, also had its influence from the capital of Bosnia-Herzegovina being Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Political identities were being, political parties were perhaps being able to be expressed or adopted by people for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that is the case, yes, starting to be that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Starting to be, and they were identifying themselves with one cause or another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a cause, with a leader, with an idea, stumbling to try to understand what is democracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to the SDS you have told us a lot about that over the last few days. I would like to ask you now about the SDA because that was active in the Prijedor area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct they had 30 seats in the Prijedor assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and very much identified by those from the Muslim background as being their party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, many Muslims must obviously have voted for other parties, otherwise the percentage would have been higher. There were also a few known Serbs who voted for this party. I shall not go into names, but they were later to be found among the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I put a very general question to you there about the them identifying essentially the SDA with the Muslim party. Do you disagree with that or not? You said that a few Serbs may have voted for it. You said that some Muslims voted for other parties. But its identification was very much with the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The local people in Prijedor who supported this party were also campaigning on its behalf, both the parties, the SDS and the SDA, were, so to speak, locked in a political battle for control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, but I would take this opportunity to point out that in contradistinction to the Serb party the Muslims had everything to win to keep unity between the different ethnic groups at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
