utterances.text: Yes, but that does not prevent people from campaigning on behalf of their party and adopting the causes of their party, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think that is the rule of the game in terms of democracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the Serb people, whether they had been told rightly or wrongly, believed that the Muslim identity was a threat to them; that is what they believed, the local people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The polarization of these two communities starts to take place, one side identifying with one particular party, the other identifying with the other party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, I think it has to be seen as being a distinction. I fully agree that the Serbs started to feel very fearful of the non-Serb due to the propaganda. I do, however, think still the Muslims, from what can be recorded from this period, had everything to gain from peaceful harmonious relationships and I think this was reflected in the general thinking of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say you think that it was reflected in the general thinking of the people. That may not necessarily have been the case, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will agree, but I would like to tell you that one of the surprising things that have come up from witness statements -- and I assume I do not have the same limitations now to answer your questions as I imposed on myself previously in terms of what I am entitled to refer to and not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is a matter for the Court really over the issue of how far you are able to go into information that others have told you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know what the witness is referring to. I think perhaps what she is saying is that now she is on cross-examination and the rules perhaps change a little bit. Let me see what happens and then if you object as it being non-responsive or not supported, I will hear it. I do not know exactly what she is saying, although I think I understand what she is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my statement was general so far; it may be more important later. One of the things that comes true and that has surprised me with the testimonies we have seen from more than or close to 400 that was arranged under my supervision and the rest we received from the US, the UK, France, Denmark Switzerland, is actually that the Muslim community seems to have been taken by surprise when it comes to the extent of violence and confrontation. It seems as if they were perhaps considering that it could be a difficult period, perhaps considering there could be fighting, but they had not, I believe, in general imagined any of this which speaks, I think and I think you will hear this from witnesses later, speaks to the fact that I do not think the SDA and the campaign for the SDA has been waged, and there is no information which contradicts this on a basis on which the other groups were presented as real threats, physical threats. Political opponents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just to make it clear so that we understand how you are in a position to give this evidence, you refer to witness statements that have been the statements taken from various people and provided to you. They have been taken through interpreters, presumably, and put into your language ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- or into English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into English, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So they have been taken through interpreters by someone else and then provided to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, and that obviously opens up for the answers that may have been left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, the source of your information comes through others. You say that from your reading of these statements you get the impression that people were surprised by what happened, and that is on the basis of what you have been told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. I should also add that at the end of the Prijedor research project, so to speak, I was approached by a number of Serbs, including people living in, having lived in Banja Luka, people living in, having lived in Belgrade, and, as mentioned earlier, every source we were searching through confirms this impression. So it is primarily the witness statements which, yes, have been taken through translators, but it is corroborated by all other available information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: These statements have been taken after these events have happened some time later and when these two groups have become even more polarized because of the events that have happened in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct that they have been taken afterwards, but it may surprise you to learn that I feel they have not all become that polarized, because the surprising thing is when you speak to people from Prijedor of non-Serb origin, your Honours, they beg to come back home and when you say to them, "Can you go back home to live with the Serbs in Prijedor?" they look at you and go blank and say, "Of course we can. It was not my neighbour in general who turned against me. Yes, some did, but they were misled, misguided. We had no ethnic hatred. This was a war which was organised, it was systematic, it was widespread, but it was not originated from within Prijedor." They want to go back and live together. Also the Serbs who approach us say, "Let's find the truth. We will help you seek for the truth. Only by seeking out those who were responsible can we in the future live together and that is what we wish and that is what we want."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I ask you then about some of the things that may have taken place that you may or may not know about, you may not have been told about them, I do not know, for instance, roadblocks in areas where the Muslim people were in the majority. We heard your evidence yesterday that referred to a roadblock at Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where there had been a shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There two Serb people had been killed at the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said they may be Eagles or Wolves; I was not quite sure which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bijeli Orlovi being White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But possibly it was not something you particularly knew about from your own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the people who were involved in that particular shooting incident has given that information. That is my basis for saying so. I have not seen it acknowledged anywhere to which group they belong. It is not stated in the papers when they are honouring the people within their own Brigades mentioned, etc., that these two people have been honoured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. They have not been described anywhere as having been Eagles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, but they have also not been described as belonging to any of the other official entities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They have not to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not as belonging to the police, not as belonging to the 343rd Motorized Brigade, not as belonging to the 11th Partisan Brigade; not as belonging to the 6th Sana Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What we take from this, then, is that there is a roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And free passage is being prevented into Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In terms of passage with weapons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In terms of passage into Hambarine, this would have been an illegal roadblock, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it would not have been an illegal roadblock. It has to be considered that those who took power in Prijedor by armed force and violence on 30th of April 1992 rebelled against the legal government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we just examine that. As I understood it, this was a bloodless coup on 30th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By armed force but without a bullet fired according to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, from all accounts, not with violence; it was an armed takeover but not with violence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What we have in this roadblock at Hambarine is any authority from anyone to set it up? Any power from Sarajevo or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police officials and the TO officials who had by this not given up power, if they had not the majority had most probably done that, may have acted as they deemed appropriate within their legal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, it was a combination of the police and the Territorial Defence, was it, in Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not my answer. I was answering that both, some police and some representatives of the TO may not yet have ceased to function. That is what was illustrated also with the takeover in Ljubija on 22nd of May when the Serb authorities said they achieved a takeover with a bloodless, well, a bloodless takeover once again. I did not address who were the people at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, I am sorry, I thought you were rather indicating that it was a legal roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was saying that it could be police, it could be TO, that is, it could be representatives of legal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It could be anything, but could be's do not make it legal, would you not agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there is a big distinction between what may be documented as having been the case, and we may perhaps not be able to do this at this point as evidence in court, but I am saying that if it is established in retrospect that this was either police or TO, they still had authority from legally elected, a legally elected government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There were other roadblocks as well that were organised by Muslim groups in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Kozarac itself had a roadblock off the main road to prevent people entering into Kozarac without being checked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my understanding that people were not allowed to enter into the area with arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that is your understanding, but what you have is a roadblock where people are armed at the roadblock into Kozarac; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and again the authority to put such a roadblock there came from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Either the police or the TO if they were authorised, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if they were authorised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am saying that if it was TO or if it was police they were, yes, legal representatives of a legal authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So what we have here in a microcosm in a small example is roadblocks that are controlling what is happening in that particular area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have now referred to two roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that means that you think these two roadblocks controlled the area, well, that is a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right, but you are here as an expert witness to advise us on what was taking place in Prijedor. Can you tell us about other Muslim roadblocks that there may have been that you can name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was allegations that there was a roadblock in Jakupovici which I may point out to you on the map, if I could have that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 79.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can in the meantime indicate to your Honours that initially Serb officials would report there had been roadblocks (in the plural) on the road from Prijedor to Banja Luka. Later they said there was one such roadblock. This was the time when they were moving through a lot of heavy equipment and tanks, etc.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want the witness to use Exhibit 79, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the witness asked to have it before her so that she could point it out to the court, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you still need it, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps not. It is to explain about where it is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was going to say it is very simple just to explain where it is. It is very near Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not say "very near" but it is not far away. It is closer to Lamovita but it is within that area and it is on the main road and, depending on what we consider far and near, we may agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But it is very easy to see on the map near Kozarac. Again, these were Muslim roadblocks which were also being established in the name of the SDA, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my knowledge, not in the name of the SDA but in the name of the legally elected authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But was not there an assertion by the Muslim population of their identity and their right, and I make no criticism of this, that they were identified with the SDA and they were acting in the name of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may make a comparison. I would assume in any one country if there is a group who want to rebel by armed force, if people then want to rally round the legal authorities, I think they will go for the lawfully legally elected authorities and not for a body. It is my firm understanding that they are rallying round and supporting the lawfully elected government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are saying it then was not an assertion particularly identified with one of the political parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am saying it was people standing up for their lawfully elected government in which the SDA, the party of the Democratic Action, played an important role but it was not the key element. The element was a lawfully legally elected government as recognised by the world community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The TO, Territorial Defence, in these areas such as Kozarac and Hambarine, at this stage in 1992 were primarily consisting of the local Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may I would like just to introduce your Honours to the background of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could just answer the question, first of all, and if it needs to be followed up we can do so, but I have asked you the question and, if possible, I would like you to answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it has to be kept in mind that the TO was part of high school education, university -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Kay wants you to answer to the extent that you can "yes" or "no" and then, of course, explain. Is that what you want Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can you answer "yes" or "no" and then you may explain as much as you consider appropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I consider appropriate, your Honours, to state that those who lived in an area would automatically be members of the TO in that area. Tito was running the former Yugoslavia under a slogan "Let us live so as if we will have peace for 100 years and do not consider there may be war tomorrow". So people's self-defence and community self-protection was the subject taught at every high school, it was as Marxism of obligation for every one student, meaning that even students second and third year of high school 15, 16 years old, would be starting to be enlisted in the TO. This was part of the total defence approach whereby everyone was called upon to be party, to defend their country. So everyone, girl and boy, living in an area from adolescence onward would be enrolled in the TO of that area, regardless of ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us take Kozarac itself. Do you know how many people were in the TO in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would assume that, again I do not have exact numbers, but to my understanding the TO in Kozarac was set up exactly the same way as elsewhere. Those women would not -- adult women would not serve in the TO. Those who served in the armed forces or were Reserves or were in the police or the police reserve, would not serve in the TO. But there was a likelihood of most males not being in either one of those two units, police or military, having reached maturity being either straight in the TO or some kind of -- in a position to be called into the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1992 do you know how many non-Muslims at the start of that year were in the TO in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the exact numbers, no, but again it would be every adult male living in Kozarac who was not in the armed forces, not in the Reserve, not in the police and not in the police reserve, and not for any particular physical reason exempted from that duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to males, was there not any female presence within the TO and, indeed, in the Kozarac TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As stated, young girls were all introduced to the TO and there could be the occasional service of women but, in general, the armed services in the former Yugoslavia was for the males.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it comes to this, you cannot give us any numbers concerning the TO in Kozarac, how many members it had and what the numbers of non-Muslims were within that body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing I can give you is that I assume the percentage is reflected almost by the percentage of the different ethnic groups living in the area. I have no reason to indicate that there is a big discrepancy between these numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you do not know if Serbs, for instance, were excluded from being able to participate in the local TO in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. I have no information or, rather, I have no information to that. It is my understanding that at the time of the road blocks Serbs had more or less left Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Other areas such as Hambarine, again, you cannot tell us as to the numbers of non-Muslims within that particular branch of the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again what I can tell you is that I think it is reflected by the population figures of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You do not know if non-Serbs were prevented from participating in the Hambarine TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know it, but I have read carefully the Kozarski Vjesnik series of articles of how they took power in the Ljubija area -- it is six, seven articles -- and there are no such references to this having been a problem. The references would be that Serbs have been mobilized already to join different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The TO in this district of opstina Prijedor had also been mobilized, had it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think again it depends on what period we talk about. It is correct that the TO again was being called upon just prior to the conflict, but I think that is an answer that must be read in the context. If my memory serves me right, I think I would like to call on page 50 in Dr. Gow's exhibit from General Kadijevic to put this into a context, because the TO had been considered by the former authorities, or legally elected authorities, in the former Yugoslavia as being a possible obstacle. So they had been entirely deprived of their weapons and as General Kadijevic, who left office I think due to age and health reasons in January 1992, establishes when he writes his book in Belgrade in 1993, it had been efficiently ruled out as any serious threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have given there a reference but I think you have quoted reference fully; I do not know whether there is any particular need for it to be put on the monitor, unless the court requires it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I do not think so, unless you would like it, Dr. Greve? It is Exhibit 30, if you need to find it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps so that we can see? I mean, I am not particularly sure of the page, but I think it is page 50, if I may, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We did not get all the pages. I do not know whether we got that page but I do not think we have -- yes, we have, translated text page 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The relevant reference is on page 50. Page 50 is a relevant reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that has been clarified, there is no need, your Honours. I only did not want to mislead you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with the support -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I know the context of the answer and I know the reference and how you support it. I do not think there is anything missing in your explanation and the court, of course, is free to look it up.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that page 50 supports the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The answer is the reference, yes. (To the witness): That, of course, is not dealing with our particular area here of Prijedor, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It refers in general to the TO as a possible obstacle in Bosnia and Herzegovina ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- with no exceptions made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps no exceptions were being thought of at the time; it is a general statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is more correctly to view this in the context that any one area with a Serb minority population would have a particular need for this to have been applied -- accepted and fulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I have some documents to put before you now, if I can be provided with them. What I have here is a bundle for your Honours, Mr. Tieger has one. Perhaps we can give the witness the original file. (Documents handed)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have been presented with a copy of what I presume is a bundle document counsel is referring to. However, we have been given no information about the provenance of that document, where it came from, what time period, what precisely it refers to.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What number will that be in terms of the next Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Starting at Defence Exhibit 5.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I gather Mr. Tieger is registering an authenticity objection or what, I do not know. When were you given this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This morning.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It, of course, can be marked for identification purposes if this witness can identify it. That is the first hurdle, if she can do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This witness will not be able to identify it as it is not a document from her. It is like the other documents produced by her, it is from other sources, which is why I am taking this opportunity to question her upon the matters within it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What I am saying is that before an exhibit can come into evidence, of course, it has to be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then it would be offered and then if there is a question about authenticity, I am sure I will have to deal with that. There may be another way for you to handle the questioning, but if want to do it with an exhibit, the exhibit can only come in if we pass those hurdles -- as generous and as liberal and free of technical restrictions that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand and I have that very much in mind which is why decisions were taken in relation to this last night. What I have here is a series of documents that came from Prijedor police station when the Defence visited it this year. They relate to mobilization lists of the TO in the Kozarac area with the names of the particular people concerned as well as identification of weapons and signatures. These are obviously not original documents and we were not given original documents, although the original documents were filmed within a room on video by Mr. Orie who was with me. We were only permitted to take copies of the documents. The documents themselves are lists of names for each particular region or town or village, identifying, many of them signed, who was within the TO and, as I said, referring to weapons. As this is an expert witness who was drawn widely on her sources to give her evidence and, indeed, has been frank about that which was provided to her through other sources and conducted on her behalf, and has referred to documents that were not prepared by her but supplied to her, it is our submission that these documents again may be admitted into evidence through her relating to these matters that we wish to put before her as an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is the question that I had. If she cannot identify it, then I am wondering how it can come in. I do not know how you want to use it, but it just seems to me that it is a little difficult to get in an exhibit if someone cannot identify what it is. If she can identify it -- maybe she can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I very much doubt it. I am sure that this is not a document she would ever have seen, and the history and its provenance I have told the court and how we had to obtain it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you are suggesting then that this, perhaps, is something that she should have seen that should have formed the basis of her opinion, then the way for you to do it is to have it marked for identification purposes; ask her if she can identify it and then, of course, she cannot identify it, then at some other point you will be able to establish the fact that she was unable to identify documentation that you consider to be very relevant and important in her forming an opinion. That is my point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour has given a very good route and I understand the approach of the court. Perhaps a copy of it -- I am sorry, Mr. Tieger wishes to address the court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We do not wish to make this more complicated than necessary. The Prosecution is certainly prepared to accept the representations of Defence counsel in so far as the provenance ---

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Authenticity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- of this document, yes. Issues of relevance and related issues, of course, remain in so far as weight is concerned, but we certainly accept his representations in that respect.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So there is no objection as to authenticity?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is very proper of Mr. Tieger, considering the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be marked as Exhibit 5, I understand, is the next exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will you mark for that identification purposes as Defence Exhibit 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was originally set up for the computerisation of the court. There are numbers in the top right-hand corner which will have been on the computer screen under those numbers. Perhaps a copy can be put before each of the learned judges?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Again I suppose my concern is that it needs to be identified by a witness and then it would then be considered, at least, for admission into evidence after it had been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So we are now at the first hurdle. Let us see if we can get to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. Before counsel begins, for housekeeping purposes, I am advised that there may already be a document marked as Exhibit 5.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it was, 5A, B and C or something, there was an exhibit. There sure was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are we on D6? I cannot remember when we first produced the documents whether we were giving -- the Defence want a prefix of "D".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "D" for Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is for sure. What Mr. Tieger is saying is there is an Exhibit 5. As I recall, there was a 5A, B and C, I think, and so now the "D" we are referring to is D6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, D6. (To the witness): On the first page of this document -- please take the opportunity to flick through it, Dr. Greve.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started doing that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: While we have been chatting, you have been looking at it and you have before you what has been marked for identification purposes as D6, Defence 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you identify it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, the cover of this document is not part of the content but was part of a folder that it came in. I do not know whether you are familiar with the Serbian language at the front of the document to describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As earlier stated to the court, I do neither read nor speak the Serbo-Croatian language; that is neither when it is in the Latin alphabet and especially not when it is in the Cyrillic alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the second page is, in fact, the title called "List of mobilization" which the Defence have had translated and inserted there. Your Honour will see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that was on the cover, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If one turns to the first page of lists, you see there various names and Stab to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just turning over the pages rapidly, you see again further lists of names with the front page of each list often with a place, Kalate, Trnopolje, Benkovici, Kasovici. I am just giving the witness the opportunity, your Honour, to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am flicking through it. I see long lists of names from and also associated with areas in the larger Kozarac area. I see that on a number of these people it is listed weapon by the side of the name. I see no date listed to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I ask when it is dated?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is not a date so ......

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Maybe we will take an early recess, five minutes early, for counsel for the Defence and counsel for the Prosecution to get together. Perhaps we can resolve this exhibit. The Prosecution has indicated that they have no objection as to authenticity; you still though seem to have a problem with identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you want to use the exhibit with the witness, it has to be identified, I suppose, and it has to come into evidence by someone. Perhaps you can meet with the Prosecution and the two of you can reach some agreement as to how it may come in, otherwise this exhibit, perhaps, can come in at a later date and be properly identified. Then you may want to then call Dr. Greve back to ask her questions about this exhibit. To avoid that ---

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can avoid that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- perhaps the two of you can get together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There is no need to get together. We can avoid that and we will stipulate it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good, then we will stand in recess until 2.30. The purpose though of my asking you to get together is to avoid a problem with identification that you are going to have, Mr. Kay, with this witness getting this document in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am aware of that, and I think it is fair to give her an opportunity to look at it as she is on the witness stand at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is not my real concern. I would like her to have a lot of time to look at it but, more importantly, I would look for the Prosecution and the Defence to get together to see if, perhaps, the document can be admitted even though it is has become apparent that this witness will not be able to identify it. Talk about that over the noon recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (Luncheon Adjournment) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, are you ready to proceed or do you want to wait a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the stage of the luncheon adjournment -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why do we not wait just one moment? Mr. Orie is conferring with Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged to your Honour. Before the luncheon adjournment, we had reached the documents that were produced by the Defence as D6. Mr. Tieger has spoken to me at the luncheon adjournment. There is no objection from the Prosecution to the production of these documents and putting them to the witness at this stage in the proceedings. She has now had an opportunity over the luncheon adjournment herself to familiarise herself with those documents. (To the witness): Is that right, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So Defence Exhibit 6 then is admitted without objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour. There is no objection as to the foundation.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection as to the foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. Of course, we reserve argument with respect to its weight.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. The Defence Exhibit 6 will be admitted. MR. KAY (To the witness): It may be appropriate at this stage to familiarise the court with it as it is a new document. Dr. Greve, as we dealt with very briefly before the luncheon adjournment, the first page of this document has on the second page a translation in English of those words, a list of mobilization, which you can see. Thereafter, if we start at the first page which has as a reference in the top right-hand corner A/1/2, there is a list of names numbered from 1 to 28. You have a little bit of familiarity with Serbo-Croat, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the extent that I am able to identify names and to the extent that I am able to identify the abbreviations, some of them, and some of the weaponry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is what I thought. We see "STAB TO KOZARAC", "STAB TO" I said which is the Anglisization of "TO" which stands for Territorial Defence, TO, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, "Stab", are you familiar with that word meaning "staff"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the Krizni Stab and similar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are working on the same level.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you may be much more able than me. I can only humbly excuse myself for not being familiar with names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do not count on it. "STAB TO KOZARAC". Then we have stamped on this document "TO BIH", standing for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I agree on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And "STO KOZARAC". On that page we merely have a list of names as I said on A/1/2. Moving to the next page of A/1/3, whereas the previous page was a handwritten list of names obviously in the same handwriting, this is a typed out list of names; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. It is added to it, as far as I can see, some signatures and there are something written in addition on occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we see next to the names a line and there may be a signature or there may not be and, as you also point out, there are other words on it that indicate weapons such as "pistole"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We also see at the top of the page "Teritorijalna Odbarin BiH", Bosnia-Herzegovina, so the Territorial Defence, Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, "STAB TO KOZARAC" again with a stamp. There are also the words on the right-hand side, "VOD SUSICI"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Susici is a village in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with where it is on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to look, I have seen it, but perhaps I can see it if it is worth using time on that, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not want to enter into some sort of exercise or test on geography, but Susici is a place in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the name, but I am not immediately to be able to point where it is, but I accept your words that it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We do not want to take up too much time on that. Turning over to A/1/4, again the names continue with the numbering that has proceeded from the previous page. Again there are additional names written in by hand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We see again Susici in the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A/1/5, "Staff of the Territorial Defence Kozarac" with a stamp and, obviously, that is my translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "Trnopolje" which we all are familiar with as being a place in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Again lists of names and signatures or writing by some of them, if not all of them, and again mention on occasion against a name, "pistole M48, pistol"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And A1.6 is a continuation of that previous page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again with the list of names, not all the names have a signature against them or a name written against them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Various writing. A/1/7 is a continuation of that page listing down to 106 where the list ends against the name of Sejmenovic Mevludin -- apologies for my pronunciation -- but again a continuation of that previous page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With references to "pistole" "puska" and "lovacka"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. I do not know the exact meaning of the letter mentioned, but it is correct that it is listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. As we turn to A/1/8, again Territorial Defence Bosnia-Herzegovina Staff TO Kozarac, Kalata, a further list of names with signatures, but a rather fuller column on the right-hand side dealing with perhaps extra weaponry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That continues on page A/1/9 and on the third page, A/1/10, where it is handwritten as a supplement to that list down to No. 80 in the list of names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I only noticed that this one, in contra distinction to many of the other pages, has not any official stamp on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That is right. I do not know whether your copy is like mine which is taken off at the top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is -- but I have gone through this carefully and I may say that there are many pages that lack this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. As we turn to A/1/11, we see the stamp again referring to Trnopolje Elezi, again the Territorial Defence Bosnia-Herzegovina, lists of names with various signatures against most of the names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On A/1/12, that page continues with the stamp, however, at the end. A/1/13 has handwritten in the top right-hand corner Kamicani, another district within opstina Prijedor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a village, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A village, yes, sorry, another village within opstina Prijedor. We again see lists of names with either signature or writing next to it and references to various weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "Pistole automatska". That page continues on to A/1/14 where the list there ends at 62 with the stamp, but on A/1/15 there is handwritten continuation of that list but, as you correctly noticed before, this is a page that is without a stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I am not able to read the numbers to make or to be sure that this is a continuation of the previous page. It could possibly be, but these are left out on mine and I have, when going through this document, seen that these listed numbers lack pages, may jump in pages, may add numbers. It is very inconsistent the way it is being presented, if I may point that out?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I will not take any criticism from us in relation to that. We are presenting it as it was actually given to us in a bundle which I think may assist the court. We have not altered any page order in relation to this document. It is just as it came. The best original version of this document, in fact, has 63 in the top left-hand corner and the previous page, A/1/14, the last number is 62. So, 63 appears to be a continuation and, like my photocopy, your photocopy may be missing that vital "6"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If I may say, it was not intended as any criticism, only an observation since I was asked to go through this carefully and I have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. A/1/16, again we see the familiar form, Kotlova, again another village ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may well be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As it is under the Stab in Kozarac, it must be in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and we see a list of 21 names only on that page and again, as you have mentioned, the stamp is on that page. Menkovici at A/1/17, that list continues listing some 130 names, perhaps even slightly more, up to page 20?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wonder what is the meaning of Menkovici? It could be a village again, but I am not fully familiar with that. There are not all the villages that are listed, but possibly one could check this against the census and where people are registered. The good census, the readable one, will have this and was an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Menkovici is just south of Kozarac, some five kilometres south, I think, a few kilometres south. We then have at page 21 a list of names, 1 to 7, but without any more specific identification of area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also true, and it is a general characteristic that there are included a number of pages with no reference to area or not in sequence with previous pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. But on that page it certainly mentions a nine millimetre pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Turning to page 22, Stari Grad, presumably you know where Stari Grad is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the old town and it is not in Kozarac. So I have difficulties in understanding that Stari Grad is listed by the TO in Kozarac. It is in Prijedor town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Stari Grad was also a district of Kozarac; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The old town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a different Naselje, Mjesna Zajednica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As a district of Kozarac known as the old town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If there are quarters like that, I accept the word for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The words simply mean "old town" do they?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour, yes. (To the witness): We see again the familiar TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina, staff TO Kozarac and the stamp, and again a list of names with signatures and references to some weapons; and on page 123, 23, the continuation of that, 24, 25 with some 107 names, not all of which though have signatures against them or writing against them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for your convenience, I may perhaps add that there are 2,767 people listed. I may have made a calculation mistake, but that is the approximate number. I used a calculator.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In the whole exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are we going to go through this entire exhibit page by page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am going to speed it up having set the ground, your Honour. If the court wants me to do it more slowly, I will do so, but I think it is a fairly familiar document now as we go through it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do it more slowly or more quickly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If the court wanted me to take it page by page or take it more quickly. I am looking for an indication from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us see, we have gone through about a fifth of it. I would rather end it right now unless you have a reason for us to go through each and every page. MR. KAY (To the witness): Having given the witness the opportunity to look at it over the luncheon adjournment, you can confirm that again on these pages there are districts in the area of Kozarac which are named on them where these lists are contained; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we have said, with signatures as well as mention of various forms of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the format varies. On some occasion there is the sole signatures, sometimes there is not a signature, sometimes there is both the signature and the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Let us move through to page 92 where there is writing in Serbian and on the page behind on a further sheet a translation of that into English as to what the typed wording is on each section. "Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Staff of the Territorial Defence of Kozarac CALL for the general mobilization in the local commune of Kozarac which is part of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina", and then there is a space for a name: "Failure to attend this call is a punishable offence under the laws of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina", and then various stamps relating to the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kozarac and the MZ of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. May I just ask you, in the document I have been given there is no date, no signature. It could, of course, have by accident not been represented in the translation, but I find no reference to any dates; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, looking at the original here, there is no date on it. This is a photocopy of three sheets that have been put on one page in Prijedor police station. So it is actually three documents that were put on the same page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But none of these documents, I understand, then had a date on them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A date at all, no, that is right. If we move to the next page, 93 -----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I ask you something about 92?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The original has a name that comes in if one looks at the translation after the word "call", does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It comes in after the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. THE WITNESS. Yes, it is a reference to the village, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "Softic Suad".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It looks like a man's name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: "Softic Suad" would be perhaps a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: That comes in where in the original -- just before "call".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It comes after "call".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: After "call"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: So it is calling so and so, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It is after "call", the writing after "call" which has been abbreviated "TO BiH", the familiar Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then there is room for the name. (To the witness): On 92 there are other names that have been reproduced there, Senad, Softic, Nedzad. 93 is a similar kind of document with the name Softic Hasan, Softic Sead and then Eolin, it seems on the third one, Edin or Edin. Then the list again continues with other, Mahmuljini; 94 with a list of names, handwriting against those names, as in 95, 96, Garibi, as does 98 which is taking us towards the end of the document, 99 Besici, 100 Zerici, and 102 was the back page of the document as presented to us which, perhaps, can be ignored. You are quite right to refer to the fact that there are no dates on these documents. Presumably, they will not have been documents that you will have seen in your research?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have seen a footage presentation of some pages as Radio Televizija Banja Luka on one occasion did show lists of names and weapon attached, but I am not able to recall if it was any of these specific lists and names. It is among the documents I have been searching for as it was frequently referred to as vital documentation by journalists but they were never entitled to get copies. I tried to get copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are people who are living and some who are allegedly killed on these lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right. So you will have seen this document or something that looks similar to it within television footage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would assume that I possibly have done that. I do not dispute that this is a document that you have obtained from the police station in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. As far as the documents are concerned, they show lists of names for the Territorial Defence for various villages in this area around Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the way they can be read, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That is all I ask on this subject and we can move now from that. I just want to move now to the time of the conflict and the shelling of Kozarac as you described it on 24th May. The terms of your evidence were that it appeared to be on all sides, be it from the mountains behind Kozarac, or from artillery positions that were further south perhaps the other side of the large lake fish farm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And maybe even other regions as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. That is to the west and the east ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And shelling that was liable to hit any property within Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which could absolutely hit almost any property. It was aimed at the villages and at areas on the mountain side, the foot of the mountain, where people were seeking refuge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the weaponry we are talking about is what kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is heavy weaponry, artillery, mortars, howitzers, this kind of -- grenade launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, that can land anywhere, as you have rightly said, and damage any sort of property within that district?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, but I also think ballistic knowledge from those operating these weaponry is sophisticated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are not talking here about ammunition that can be specifically guided; it when fired is less precise than any guided kind of missile through modern technology?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. There are weaponry with much higher or a much better ability to target them and get the target, but also these weapons were aimed at targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, targeting this particular area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And possibly areas within the area more than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to the services, you said that services such as electricity were cut off for non-Serb people, but all people lost their services such as electricity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may remind that I also said that before the real attack on Kozarac, essentially, all Serbs had left or the majority of Serbs had left. If they had been in the area they would have had exactly the same difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Unless you had a battery radio to receive Radio Prijedor or other radio stations, the electricity for the television had gone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But there were radios operating, yes. That was a means of communication, that was the one of the means used for the ultimatum, to my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But that would have been radio that operated off battery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Or some supplemental form of energy rather than plugging it into the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just one other again general matter: you have referred to the camps of Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje. I just have a very few, short questions to ask about those matters. First of all, Keraterm: is it correct that there were, in fact, offices operating within this large complex, it is a large building Keraterm, this ceramics factory which also had offices within it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct that Keraterm was a large building. It is also correct that when former detainees are making a map of this camp, they are putting in a question mark as to what was the actual use of certain areas to which they had no access.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It is a building that has the means for making ceramics and for storage of the appropriate materials for their manufacture that was on a fairly large scale, a fairly large factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, and the part that was used for the camp were four halls which was only one part of the entire complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But there is a side of this building where there are other offices that were used by other businesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, there is a side where there could be offices that could have been used by other offices at this time of which, however, the inmates are not clear. They were not given access to this area and has not been able to explain what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. There was just one matter I wanted to clear up with you there to give the picture of those premises which you also said were fairly close to the main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is the main road that runs from Banja Luka to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With the whole premises clearly visible from the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The outdoor part of the premises, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Omarska, you refer to people entering those camps. You said they entered at night to commit beatings and killings upon people. Were you aware of a pass that was required to be shown to enter Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There could have been passes, but I am also aware of even from Serb sources that if they wanted they could come to the camp. I do not think my testimony has limited the access for outsiders to night-time. I made a reference to this frequently happening at night-time, but it could also happen at day-time, to my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to look at some documents here, and there are copies for the Bench as well.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this is a proposed exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, it has been provided to Mr. Tieger this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It has, your Honour. It has not come back from copying. I would like to know if counsel has an additional copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do, one for the witness of each pile and one for the judges.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will mark for at that identification purposes as Defence 7. (Document handed). I have just handed two documents to you, one in the Cyrillic script of the Serbian language but written in Latin script the word "Omarska" and a name, Savic Drago, and a number and then a translation into English which the Bench will see follows the document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you wish to offer this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Has it been identified? Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do not know whether it has been identified. I assume it came from the same source as the previous document, that is, the Prijedor police station. We would treat it in the same way; we have no objection. There is no need for the Defence to go through the process of calling someone from Prijedor. We accept the -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, can you identify Defence 7? Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To me, this is an entirely new document. I will not be surprised if such a document has existed. I do not know if I should refrain from commenting on the name that appears. Possibly, it will be -- the Defence will tell us who this man is so I shall not go into that part perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This does not actually come from Prijedor police station, but from a witness whom the Defence propose to call.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As I indicated, our rules of evidence are very limited and our procedure is going to be very open. I do not know that this witness can identify it, but if there is no objection Defence 7 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there on objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, my understanding of the provenance of this document was incorrect. Since there was nothing mentioned to distinguish it from the other document, I assumed it came from the same source. Now we hear it comes from essentially somewhere, a witness, and in essence we are asking to stipulate to the admissibility of this document without knowing anything about its source, when it was created, who created it, in whose possession it was, who the person is who turned it over and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you intend to call a witness who will be able to identify this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right. This is taken from the particular section of the proof of that witness. It is being produced before this witness to give her an opportunity to deal with it as she is an expert witness and has advised the court on the circumstances of Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje. One could avoid putting it to this witness at all, but it does give her an opportunity to deal with it before we call Defence evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The only problem is identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Judge Stephen suggests that perhaps you tell us who this witness will be who will be able to identify it; that will at least put it in a frame of reference for us later on. We still have a problem with the admission of this exhibit through this witness. If this witness cannot identify the exhibit, unless the Prosecutor is willing to waive any objections and allow it to come in as whatever it may be, a piece of paper identified as Defence 7, we still have that problem of getting it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The witness producing it will be the person named on the particular document. It has no need to become an actual exhibit yet; it can be dealt with by this witness in cross-examination for any comment she may have, because she has dealt with this subject generally and we can produce it officially in the fullness of time within the Defence case when we call the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Rather than marking it as an exhibit, and I do not know exactly what you plan on doing with it, why do you not just hold it in front of you and ask the witness if she has ever heard of whatever is on the front page, if that is what you are trying to establish? She will say, no, she has never heard of that, or may be she will say, yes, or whatever. The problem is just getting the piece of paper in. It looks like it is just two pages and you can just ask Dr. Greve whether she has ever heard of whatever is on the front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and the purpose for producing it was because she dealt with the access to the camp at Omarska. I am giving her an opportunity to deal with it. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, you dealt with access to the camp at Omarska. Here I am producing a document to you with an English translation relating to an entrance permit into that camp of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that and, as I testified yesterday and the day before, people did enter (or this was only yesterday) people did enter Omarska who were staff, who were occasional staff and who were outsiders. I would not be surprised if none of these would have an entrance permit, that is to say, the ordinary staff, the occasional staff, I would find it quite reasonable they would have a permit, but I have not seen such a permit before.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. So now you have what is marked for identification purposes as Defence Exhibit 7. It has been shown to the witness and she says that she has never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It still will be a part of the record and when you intend to call this particular witness, then you can have this witness refer to what was marked for identification purposes as Defence 7 that Dr. Greve could not identify, and then ask your witness about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have accomplished your purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is something we are just producing at this stage. It saves having even to call this witness back again to deal with anything in particular. (To the witness): There we are; it is a document in a particular name with an identification card number apparently with it ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- and signed by Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, then head of the Serbian police, public security -- or, yes, it is actually signed on the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, being an entrance permit for access to the investigation centre, Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which is how you heard Omarska camp being described, as an investigation centre, I believe that is what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "military investigation centre" is the reference used normally, yes, by the Serbs. I see here it is translated as "investigation centre", I assume that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is the end of that matter. Just one other general matter as well dealing with calendars. You advised us yesterday, having considered dates and dates that may conflict, of the use of both the Gregorian and the Julian calendars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Julian calendar is a fortnight after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. But these calendars are, in fact, printed together; if you have a calendar in Bosnia-Herzegovina at this time, you would have both sets of dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not seen that. I have asked for it but not been able to obtain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So my information is from the authorised joint United Kingdom, United States of America official calendar for 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As far as the Muslim people were concerned in this area, they would have applied the Gregorian dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be it, but on occasions they would have made reference not to a date but to a particular religious feast, and then came the question who was the translator and how was this presented further on, and there could be confusion on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So dates identified by a particular event such as a religious feast is something we are all familiar with, but in daily life in Bosnia-Herzegovina the Gregorian calendar was the calendar that was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In daily life in Bosnia-Herzegovina the Gregorian calendar was used for everyday life. However, it was used by the orthodox church in Bosnia-Herzegovina as being the basis for the religious feast and, as I think has been demonstrated through some of the evidence presented or the documents brought into evidence, there are many religious feasts being celebrated and there is frequent reference to the feast rather than to the date. That is why I thought it useful as it had confused me possibly to pre-empt any confusion by just having mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just a few questions. Dr. Greve, with regard to the access document to which Mr. Kay made reference, or to the possibility of an access document, let me say that, was it your understanding that it was possible to keep people out of Omarska camp during the period of it operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume it could have been possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were certain people kept out of Omarska camp, for example, members of the ICRC during the period of its operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. There was no international access before the camp had been almost emptied in early August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about investigating journalists who might want to look into what was happening in the camp? Did the camp authorities seem to be able to keep them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. The entire area was sealed off. They could not come close to it even.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was it the understanding of those members of the media or people from international humanitarian organisations that they were being kept out because the authorities did want them to know what was going on there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was their firm understanding, yes. It is also, if I may add, the basis for many of the appeals from ICRC when they are in strong language to be an agency that normally uses diplomatic language when they are really asking access to these camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would that mean that someone who did obtain access to the camp whether by pass or not would, presumably, be someone whom the authorities in charge of the camp did not mind was in there and seeing what was going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that can be stated without reservation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there anything about the access pass that Mr. Kay mentioned that indicated that anyone who got in there had to be escorted around by responsible camp officials to see that he or she did not do anything the camp authorities did not want them to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Anything about the access document to which Mr. Kay referred that suggested that anyone who got into the camp with a pass or not would be restricted from doing anything he might want to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were asked by the Defence about shelling and how accurate mortars, cannon and artillery might be when fired from some distance; do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kay indicated that it was understandably difficult to control the precise location in which those explosions might occur; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the way I understood his question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have seen pictures and video footage of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that most, if not virtually all, of the structures in Kozarac have been destroyed, whether by the initial shelling or subsequent destruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all, as there are some marked exceptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Among those exceptions would that include the Serbian orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be one such exception, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would it also include the home and cafe of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be one such exception, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few questions about the document which was marked, if I recall correctly, as Defence 6A or D6.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The one that was marked for identification purposes only?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour, the bundle of documents, the list of names.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
